story.opening: Before dawn at Adwa, General Baratieri sends his soldiers into the Ethiopian hills. His Italian columns are supposed to support each other. Instead, they lose contact. One force becomes several isolated targets. By the time the mistake is clear, Emperor Menelik's army is closing in. Italy expected a colonial victory. It is about to suffer a catastrophe.
story.ending: An African Union-brokered agreement in Pretoria brought a cessation of hostilities in November twenty twenty-two. It was a crucial opening, not a promise that every grievance had been settled. At Adwa, Ethiopia's leaders had built unity against an invader. The harder task was making that unity work when the enemy was no longer outside the border. Survival could be won on a battlefield. Sharing a country required something the battlefield could never decide.
